Subject: Localization rulebook & offer sensitivity analysis

Team —

Attaching the second pass of the offer sensitivity workbook (sensitivity_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a short rulebook PDF (rulebook-offer-sensitivity.pdf). Goal: produce a single, operational rulebook People Ops can embed into offer templates and recruiting training by end of month. High-level asks: 

- Please review the proposed tolerance bands (tab "Tolerance") and flag any regional edge-cases.
- Check the "Escalation" flow: at what threshold do we require GC/Comp approval vs. hiring manager signoff?
- Confirm benchmark data looks reasonable against our own closed-win offers (I attached a sample).

Notes from my side: the sensitivity matrix models offer movement sensitivity to base vs. total comp, and simulates candidate acceptance probability using our internal conversion curve. I recommended a 7% band for US-SF, 10% for US-remote mid-markets, and a 15% starting tolerance for APAC hub cities (adjustable once we get local hiring velocity).

If you can get comments back by EOD Tuesday I can fold into the People Ops draft. Ella (cc'd) provided the first-pass benchmarking; she can expand on regional deltas below.

Thanks,
Alex

Thanks Alex — quick read-through and a couple of inline notes below. Attaching the geo CSV I pulled for the same roles (geo-benchmarks-2027.csv).

Inline: 
- Tolerance: SF 7% seems OK for senior ICs; for junior ICs I'd push to 5% to avoid over-indexing on geography.
- Escalation: the flow looks fine but we should add an explicit clause for "critical hiring" (hard-to-fill/platform roles) that allows a second-round CM/GM waiver at +5% beyond tolerance with VP approval.
- Cost control: can we add a recommended quantization step for Dedicated vs Hosted roles? Practically, that will help Sales hire without breaking cost guardrails.

I left comments in the workbook (column H on "Tolerance"). Happy to sync if folks want to run the scenarios together.

–Marissa

Thanks for the ping. A couple of observations from our side after running regional regressions against public comp sources and anonymized private benchmarks: 

- APAC hubs: effective bandwidth in Bangalore, Singapore shows higher variance for entry and mid levels (we recommend a 12–18% working tolerance band, driven by exchange rate and mix of local vs expatriate hires).
- LATAM: market delta vs US is compressed for remote-friendly roles — for some engineering functions a 6–8% uplift vs LATAM market median can clear candidates who have competing remote offers.
- Data caveat: our dataset has fewer closed offers in some narrow infra specialties; where sample size <30 we recommend manual bench review.

I've attached an excerpt CSV (we included the region code in geo-benchmarks-2027.csv) and flagged cells where sample size was small. Happy to join a short sync to walk the methodology.

—Ella
Principal Analyst, CompBench
Attachment referenced: geo-benchmarks-2027.csv

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Localization rulebook & offer sensitivity analysis — decision items

Thanks for the comments — below are the decision items I want to lock this week so People Ops can publish the rulebook: 

1) Tolerance default bands (by region): US-SF 7% (senior 7 / junior 5), US-remote 10%, APAC hubs 15% (reduce after 90-day velocity review), LATAM 8%. (Marissa: confirm you'd accept the junior adjustment)
2) Escalation thresholds: 
   - Manager +1 approval up to tolerance.
   - For offers > tolerance but <= tolerance + 5%: VP of Hiring or Comp Committee signoff.
   - For offers > tolerance + 5%: GC and CFO notice + formal exception form (rulebook annex B).
3) Critical-hire waiver: for designated "critical" roles (list maintained by Eng hiring leads) allow VP waiver up to tolerance +5% with documented business case.
4) Benchmarking caveat: regions with sample size <30 require manual bench (documented in rulebook).

If you all agree, I'll route the compiled PDF and the XLS mock-up to People Ops and Legal for inclusion in the offer generator. I also want to add a short FAQ for recruiters that covers: "When to escalate", "How to log compensatory exceptions", and "How to handle counteroffers".

Please respond with a quick +1 / -1 and any small edits by EOD today so we can move this to People Ops.

Alex
